documents.body:
## Working time – what every rota must follow

- Weekly hours: no more than 48 hours in any Monday–Sunday week, unless the person has signed the 48-hour opt-out.
- Daily rest: at least 11 hours off between the end of one shift and the start of the next.
- Weekly rest: 24 hours off in a row in every 7 days, or 48 hours in every 14 days.
- Breaks: every shift over six hours has at least 20 minutes' break (already built into our shifts).
- Night workers: no more than 8 hours' work on average per 24 hours.
- Staff records are binding: nobody works on a fixed day off, outside a nights-only contract or during a recorded absence (sick calls included).
- Each staff record shows the maximum number of nights per month for that person.
- Nights in a row, the nurse minimum per shift, working days in a row, late-to-early and part-time margins: see the current house rules and the signed works agreement.
- Staffing at night: a nursing home has at least one registered nurse on duty at all times, by night as by day.
- A course or mandatory training day is working time: it counts as a working day of 7.5 hours for days in a row, the part-time limit and the weekly hours.

## Shift times and breaks

| Shift | Start | End | Break |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Early | 06:00 | 14:00 | 30 minutes |
| Late | 14:00 | 22:00 | 30 minutes |
| Night | 22:00 | 06:00 | 30 minutes |

### Which rule applies?
If two written sources disagree, the order is: law, then the signed works agreement, then the current house rules, then memos. An expired memo does not apply. If two valid memos disagree, the newer one applies.
documents.title: Staff handbook (extract): working time

documents.body:
## House rules for the rota

- Minimum staffing per unit (house standard for a unit of 25 residents, care staff only): early 4, late 3, night 1; a dementia unit has 1 more by day (its team leader). Each unit's numbers follow its residents and are in the rota demand.
- No more than 4 night shifts in a row.
- At least 1 registered nurse on every early and late shift on every unit. At night one registered nurse is on duty for the whole home; she or he is rostered on Maple Wing, and the other units' night cover may be a care assistant.
- No more than 6 working days in a row.
- No early shift the morning after a late shift.
- Part-time staff may work at most 10% above their contract hours in a Monday–Sunday week.
- Swap requests for shifts today or tomorrow are not approved; the office arranges cover instead.

Where the signed agreement or the law says otherwise, that applies (order of sources: see the staff handbook).
